 FILE — Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas demonstrates a new voter tabulating machine in Hartford, CT on Nov. 3, 2025. The state will audit last week’s election results in 49 precincts. Credit: Donald Eng / CTNewsJunkie 
 HARTFORD, CT — Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas’ office has selected 49 precincts from last week’s general election to have their machine totals audited. Post-election audits are a routine safeguard designed to ensure votes are counted accurately, the office said in a statement.
 In addition to the 49 precincts, selected by die rolls, the office also selected 17 alternates.
 “We don’t wait to hear about something going wrong before we go back and check our results,” Thomas said. “I’ve talked all election season about people, paper, and proof. Now we’re at the paper and proof stage: going back to our paper ballots and checking whether the machines counted them accurately.”
 Connecticut General Statutes § 9-320f requires that 5% of all voting precincts have their machine totals audited. There were 973 precincts used during the election.
 Bipartisan local election officials in the 49 selected precincts will now re-tabulate the voter-marked paper ballots and compare those results with what the tabulators reported on Election Day.
 Officials in the selected precincts must complete their audits by November 23. The reports will then be forwarded to UConn for independent analysis. The university’s findings will be returned to the Secretary’s Office and filed with the State Elections Enforcement Commission, Thomas said. The findings will also be made available to the public.
